questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How social media affects teenagers' health
How to make money on social media
Why most teenagers now prefer Snapchat to TikTok
How schools teach computer skills
questions.why: Beth says they'll be discussing how social media affects teenagers.

questions.q: What does Beth say about her own social media use?
options: She is completely addicted
She never uses social media
She only ever uses social media for work, never for fun
She isn't addicted, but uses it more than she'd like
questions.why: She says she doesn't think she's addicted but spends more time on it than she would like.

questions.q: What did research in the US find?
options: Social media makes teenagers happier
Most teenagers use social media for about one hour a day
Over three hours a day doubles the risk of depression
Adults are more affected than teenagers
questions.why: Adolescents on social media over three hours a day have double the risk of depression and anxiety.

questions.q: What have teenagers revealed in surveys?
options: They want more adverts
Many regularly see hateful content
They feel better about their bodies
They rarely use their phones at night
questions.why: Beth says 64% of teens said they are regularly exposed to hate-based content.

questions.q: What worries Professor Devi Sridhar about algorithms?
options: They show too many news stories
They keep feeding harmful content to young girls
They make phones slower
They stop teenagers from finding real friends offline
questions.why: She says young girls are being fed eating-disorder content in an addictive way.

questions.q: According to Professor Sridhar, why do apps try to keep users on their phones?
options: Their money comes from advertising
Governments ask them to
Users pay for every minute
They want to collect data about schools
questions.why: She says the vital message is that their revenue comes from advertising.

questions.q: What does Professor Sridhar say about parents?
options: They are not interested in the problem
They should ban phones completely
They spend far too much time online on their own phones
They have been left to find solutions on their own
questions.why: She says the onus has been put on parents and concerned adults to find solutions on their own.

questions.q: Why does Professor Sridhar call arguing with teenagers about apps “a losing battle”?
options: Teenagers don't listen to anyone
Parents don't understand modern technology at all
Their whole social life is on these apps
The apps are too expensive to remove
questions.why: She says it's a losing battle “because it's their entire social network”.
